title: Best UK Family Days Out: Theme Parks, Zoos & Castles
description: The best family days out in the UK: theme parks, zoos, castles, free museums, safari parks and steam railways, with tips on who each suits.
h1: The best family days out in the UK
intro: From LEGOLAND to Longleat and the Natural History Museum to Alnwick Castle, here are Britain’s best-loved family days out, with real ways to save on each.

image.alt: A grey stone castle against a blue sky

blocks.title: Scout’s UK verdict
blocks.text: Mix one big paid day with a couple of free ones. Pair a theme park with a free museum or beach day and the holiday budget goes much further.
facts: Studio Tour or a Merlin park

items.title: LEGOLAND Windsor Resort

image.alt: Yellow, red, blue and green toy building bricks

items.text: Built for families with children aged roughly 2 to 12: gentle coasters, driving schools, MINILAND models and plenty of hands-on play.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes
Listed on the National Rail Days Out Guide with a rail-ticket discount in 2026
Weekdays outside school holidays are usually the quietest and cheapest
items.scout: Under-3s go free, so it’s great value while they’re tiny. Check ride height limits before you promise anything!

items.title: Alton Towers Resort

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

items.text: The UK’s best-known thrill park, with big roller coasters for teens and CBeebies Land for little ones, plus a water park and hotels on site.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes (check exclusion dates)
A Tesco Clubcard Reward Partner in 2026: check the Clubcard app for current exchanges
Book online before you go: gate prices are usually the highest
items.scout: Split the day: thrill rides first while queues are short, CBeebies Land after lunch when little legs need a slower pace.

items.title: Chessington World of Adventures

image.alt: People riding a spinning fairground ride

items.text: A rare mix of family rides and a zoo in one ticket, which makes it a strong all-rounder for mixed-age families.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes
Animal areas are a calm break when queues build up
items.scout: Two days out for the price of one: plan your route around the animal talks and feeding times.

items.title: Paultons Park, home of Peppa Pig World

image.alt: A happy family running together in a sunlit garden

items.text: Peppa Pig World is a toddler favourite, and the park’s new Viking-themed land, Valgard, opened in spring 2026 with bigger rides for older kids.
saves: Not part of the Merlin pass: check Paultons’ own annual passes if you live nearby
Closed in January and on some winter dates, so check the calendar first
items.scout: Peppa Pig World is busiest first thing. Head there in the afternoon and do the rest of the park in the morning.

items.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour London – The Making of Harry Potter

image.alt: A Platform 9¾ sign for the Hogwarts Express

items.text: Walk through the real sets, costumes and props from the films, including the Great Hall, Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express on Platform 9¾.
saves: Children aged 4 and under go free, but still need a ticket
Book direct on the official site to avoid reseller mark-ups
Tickets can’t be bought on arrival, and school holidays sell out early
items.scout: Allow at least 3–4 hours. Save room for Butterbeer, and don’t rush the Gringotts and Hogwarts model sections at the end.

items.title: Natural History Museum

image.alt: The vaulted Hintze Hall at the Natural History Museum, London

items.text: Dinosaurs, a blue whale skeleton and an earthquake room. General admission is free.
saves: General admission is free (some special exhibitions charge)
Book a free timed slot online at busy times
items.scout: The Science Museum and V&A are next door, so you can mix and match one free day.

items.title: Chester Zoo

image.alt: Two giraffes standing side by side

items.text: One of the UK’s biggest zoos, run by a conservation charity, with a huge site to explore. Expect a full day.
saves: Book online in advance
Membership can pay off if you live nearby and visit a few times a year
items.scout: Wear comfy shoes and bring snacks: it’s a big site with lots of walking.

items.title: London Zoo

image.alt: A mother gorilla hugging her baby

items.text: The world’s oldest scientific zoo, run by the conservation charity ZSL, in Regent’s Park.
saves: Listed on the National Rail Days Out Guide in 2026 (you need valid National Rail tickets)
Combine with a free picnic in Regent’s Park
items.scout: The Days Out Guide offer needs paper or e-tickets from National Rail; Oyster and contactless don’t count.

items.title: Longleat

image.alt: A safari vehicle driving through dry bush

items.text: The UK’s first drive-through safari park outside Africa, plus a stately home, gardens and adventure play.
saves: Book online ahead
Its Festival of Light (in winter) is a separate seasonal event: check dates
items.scout: Keep windows up where the signs say so: the monkeys love a car aerial!

items.title: Edinburgh Zoo

image.alt: A visitor watching a penguin swim past the glass

items.text: A hillside zoo run by the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland, famous for its penguins.
saves: Kids Pass has listed discounts here: check the app
items.scout: It’s hilly, so a sturdy buggy or a carrier for tiny ones makes life easier.

items.title: Alnwick Castle

image.alt: A stone castle under white clouds

items.text: The castle used for Hogwarts exteriors in the first two Harry Potter films. Families can join broomstick training in the very courtyard from the movies.
saves: Check whether tickets can be upgraded to an annual pass for free on the official site
Pair with Alnwick Garden next door
items.scout: Broomstick training is pure joy for young witches and wizards. Check session times when you arrive.

items.title: The Jacobite steam train

image.alt: A steam train crossing the Glenfinnan Viaduct in the Scottish Highlands

items.text: The steam train that crosses the Glenfinnan Viaduct, famous from the Harry Potter films. It runs seasonally and sells out well ahead.
saves: You can watch the train cross the viaduct for free from the Glenfinnan viewpoints
Book as early as possible for summer dates
items.scout: Can’t get tickets? Watching it cross the viaduct from the hillside is free and just as photogenic.

sections.h2: Saving money on UK days out
sections.html: Use the National Rail 2FOR1 offers, check whether an annual pass makes sense, swap Tesco Clubcard vouchers, and plan around school holiday dates, when prices peak.

faqs.q: What is the most popular family day out in the UK?
faqs.a: Big favourites include the Natural History Museum and Science Museum (free), LEGOLAND Windsor, Alton Towers, Chester Zoo and the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London.

faqs.q: How can I save on UK attractions?
faqs.a: Travel by train and use the Days Out Guide 2FOR1 offers, consider an annual pass if you’ll visit often, look for under-5s-free rules and book online ahead of time.
